Native storage admits the typed memory injection: u32 argument IDs occupy four aligned bytes, slice lengths and pointer widths match the captured target, live lifetime IDs are unique, read-only and stack ownership are respected. Concrete native bytes and aliases match Represents/Related at operation entry.

For a nonzero request the native allocator returns OOM or a suitably aligned, bounded region disjoint from live allocations; contents are uninitialized, old allocations are framed, and private allocator effects are threaded in actual call order. Zero-size allocation/free require no live sentinel. Reuse of dead addresses does not reuse lifetime IDs.

Native memcpy and Allocator.dupe implement exact typed copying for initialized source, writable equal-length destination and nonoverlapping ranges. Dupe allocates first and preserves ordinary OOM. No implicit rollback or cleanup is assumed for a violated memory contract.

Native free consumes the whole live persistent allocation with the matching allocator, invalidates its aliases, frames other storage and preserves the actual allocator effects; zero-size release is a no-op. Caller cleanup after transfer is a separate obligation.

Native stack storage and call frames satisfy captured layout, freshness and lifetime contracts. Finite proof observation exhaustion is not native OOM or termination; machine resource exhaustion is explicit and outside normal successful execution.
The independent Solidity/Yul/EVM semantic models faithfully describe their explicitly admitted language constructs and fork. This does not assume that any compiler pass preserves those semantics.

The admission/parser and orchestration bind the exact source bytes, settings, compiler result, fork and installed runtime to the theorem. Strict schema/hash checks reject mismatches; hashes alone are not correctness proofs.
